name: Isolated SFX Design Pass
use_when: The edit feels visually polished but sonically flat.
A dense motion edit needs whooshes, risers, impacts, clicks, typing, texture, or comedy sounds.
The editor needs to focus on SFX placement without being distracted by voiceover and music.
avoid_when: Dialogue timing or visual motion is not locked enough for SFX placement.
Muting other tracks would cause the editor to ignore dialogue masking risk and skip the full-mix check.
The project tone requires sparse natural sound rather than designed SFX.

timeline_pattern.pattern: lock_visible_motion -> mute_dialogue_music_temporarily -> watch_for_sfx_moments -> place_whoosh_riser_impact_texture -> unmute_full_mix -> lower_and_fade_sfx -> final_loudness_qc
timeline_pattern.isolation_rule: Temporarily muting other tracks can help identify visual moments that need sound, but the full mix must be checked afterward.
timeline_pattern.basic_family_rule: Start from whoosh, riser, and impact families, then add context-specific sounds only when they fit the beat.
timeline_pattern.level_rule: Lower SFX after placement so they support the edit without becoming annoying.

motion.rule: SFX should match visible motion starts, impacts, transitions, text pops, or texture beats.

sound.rule: Layer and vary SFX deliberately, then use gain and fades to keep dialogue and music pleasant.

captions.rule: Do not let SFX masking force captions to carry normally intelligible dialogue.

color.rule: No direct color rule; bright flash overlays with SFX still need readability checks.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use separate SFX tracks in an EDL, apply afade and volume filters, then run loudness/waveform checks after reintroducing dialogue and music.
implementation.remotion: Trigger SFX from motion event frames and store fullMixChecked after dialogue/music are restored.
implementation.blender: Use audio markers for visual impacts, then export stems or markers for final mix.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Temporarily mute voice/music, place SFX, unmute, lower volumes, and add short fades.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Mute dialogue/music only for SFX spotting, place SFX on separate tracks, then unmute all tracks, lower clip gain, fade edges, and check speech clarity.

common_mistakes: Doing the isolated pass and forgetting to re-check the full mix.
Leaving SFX too loud because they sounded exciting when soloed.
Adding SFX to every small movement until the edit becomes tiring.
Using the same whoosh, riser, or hit repeatedly with no variation.
qc: Were dialogue and music restored after the isolated SFX pass?
Does each SFX cue match a visible motion, impact, reveal, or story beat?
Do SFX peaks stay below dialogue?
Do all SFX edges have fades or clean cuts?
